scenes.title: Define delivery scope
scenes.narration: Start with the refined offer. State what would actually be delivered and distinguish prototype, manual trial and production service. A convincing demo does not establish that you can deliver reliably.

scenes.title: Map requirements
scenes.narration: List skills, workflow, technology, partners and access needed. Mark confirmed facts separately from assumptions. Estimate effort and cost categories with source status; do not invent a complete budget or capacity proof.

scenes.title: Describe credible risks
scenes.narration: A useful risk describes a cause, possible event and consequence. For example, unconfirmed organiser access may delay the test and prevent relevant participation. Identify who is affected and which parts remain uncertain.

scenes.title: Prioritise with reasons
scenes.narration: Consider impact, likelihood or uncertainty and urgency, with reasons. Unknown does not mean low risk. Avoid a numerical total that implies safety; focus on blockers and evidence needed before proceeding.

scenes.title: Assign controls and checks
scenes.narration: Assign a proposed prevention or response, an owner and a way to check it. A written mitigation is not proof that the risk is controlled. Resolve access, privacy and specialist-review needs before execution; pause if safeguards remain unresolved.

scenes.title: Write the review
scenes.narration: Create your Feasibility and Risk Review with requirements, resource assumptions, priority risks, controls, blockers and next check. This is a founder planning review, not technical certification, legal compliance or production approval.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: A good idea still needs a deliverable plan.

children: Feasibility
asks whether you can deliver the defined scope with available capabilities and constraints. A
risk
is an uncertain event with consequences. A
blocker
is an unresolved condition that prevents the next step from proceeding responsibly.
Define the refined offer and delivery boundary.
List people, workflow, technology, partner and access requirements.
Record time/capacity/cost assumptions with sources and unknowns.
Describe credible risks as cause → event → consequence.
Prioritise by reasoned impact, likelihood/uncertainty and urgency.
Assign proposed controls, owners, checks and stop/pause conditions.
Demand versus delivery
A customer signal does not prove delivery capability. A working prototype does not prove reliable production operations, security or scalable economics.
Unknown versus low risk
Unverified access, capacity or safeguards remain unknown. A mitigation written in a worksheet is a proposal until its effectiveness is checked.
Illustrative planned risk

Cause: organiser access is unconfirmed. Event: the planned test cannot reach relevant participants on time. Consequence: evidence remains unavailable and the review is delayed. Priority: resolve before recruitment. Proposed control: responsible owner confirms a permitted route. Evidence: documented approval/status. Stop: no recruitment while access is unresolved. This is a plan, not confirmed approval.

Review risks across delivery/operations, technology, partner dependence, resources, customer harm, data handling and specialist obligations where relevant. Do not assign invented budgets, safe scores or compliance status. Record a resource category as unknown if no reliable estimate exists.

This lesson is a founder planning review. Appropriate technical, privacy, legal, financial or other specialist review may be needed for the actual venture; the worksheet does not provide certification. Use anonymous planning summaries only. No system audit, source verification or production approval is connected.
